details: PLAUSIBLE: the leftover registry state is CONFIRMED (read live, read-only); what Claude Code does with `marketplace add` of a folder already
registered under another name, and whether an installed plugin with no enabledPlugins key still loads, is not measured (needs a run of the
claude CLI against a temporary config dir). Either outcome is wrong: a refused add leaves the owner's sessions with no relay plugins until
fixed by hand (the merge hook among them), an accepted add leaves stale installs that sync_agents keeps rewriting
(installed_plugin_dirs matches by plugin name in any marketplace) and that doctor never names.
The brief asks setup --global to remove "the four X@relay keys and the relay marketplace entry"; it does that in settings.json, the file it
names, but the transition is only clean when Claude Code's own registry follows. Size: 20 agent minutes.
evidence: core@relay [('user', None, '/Users/amidman/.claude/plugins/cache/relay/core/0.1.0'), ...]  (same for observe, delegate, front)
lib/relay_setup.py:1217: unshipped_installs skips `plugin in shipped` and considers only scope == "project".
relay doctor on the worktree: "FIX relay@amidman installed (claude plugin install relay@amidman --scope project)" x4; no line names the X@relay installs.
failing_case: This machine, after the merge: ~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json holds "relay" -> /Users/amidman/relay; installed_plugins.json holds
core@relay, observe@relay, delegate@relay, front@relay at user scope. `relay setup --global` (install(run_claude=True)) edits settings.json, then runs
`claude plugin marketplace add /Users/amidman/relay` and `claude plugin install relay@amidman --scope user` (x4).
Now: nothing removes the "relay" marketplace from Claude Code's registry or uninstalls the four X@relay installs; the same folder is added a second
time under a new name (Claude Code may refuse it as already added, and then each `plugin install X@amidman` fails because marketplace amidman
is unknown); relay doctor never reports the leftovers (unshipped_installs looks only at project-scope installs, and observe/delegate/front are
"still shipped" by folder name).
Should: after setup --global the registry holds marketplace amidman only (for that folder), X@amidman installed at user scope, no X@relay install
left, or doctor names each leftover with the command that removes it.
fix_hint: In install(), when the registry (installed_plugins.json / known_marketplaces.json) holds PRE_RENAME keys, run
`claude plugin uninstall <name>@relay --scope user` for PRE_RENAME_ALWAYS_ON and `claude plugin marketplace remove relay` before the
marketplace add; extend unshipped_installs to report user-scope @relay installs. Test with a fake claude on PATH and a temp CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.
pass_cases: 1. Fake claude on PATH recording argv; registry with marketplace relay -> <root> and core@relay at user scope; install(run_claude=True):
the recorded calls include `plugin uninstall core@relay --scope user` (and observe/delegate/front) and `plugin marketplace remove relay`,
both before `plugin marketplace add <root>`; then `plugin install relay@amidman --scope user`.
2. Same, with no X@relay in the registry and no relay marketplace: no uninstall or remove call is made; marketplace add and the four installs run as today.
3. run_claude=False: settings.json is cleaned as test_rename.GlobalSettings asserts, and the todo line names the uninstall/remove steps.
4. relay doctor with a user-scope observe@relay in the registry: one FIX line naming observe@relay and the command that removes it.
reason: tests/test_rename.py RegistryLeftovers (uninstall and marketplace remove before add; clean registry makes no call; todo names steps; doctor line). Fail at a05b43e, pass at head.
findings.summary: setup --global drops the old ids only from settings.json; Claude Code's registry keeps marketplace relay -> ~/relay and four user-scope X@relay installs, and then marketplace add is run for a folder already registered under the old name

details: CONFIRMED by reading. The exemption was added (6241137) because the gate ran from the worktree while the live PATH still held
~/relay/plugins/core/bin (core@relay enabled); after setup --global that PATH entry becomes plugins/relay/bin and the exemption is no longer
needed. It contradicts the no-backward-compatibility decision. Size: 5 agent minutes, but it can only be dropped once the live PATH has
moved (after the merge and setup --global), so listing it is acceptable.
failing_case: After the merge relay has no plugins/core. A different program installed at ~/somewhere/plugins/core/bin/kit (another marketplace's plugin
named core, shipping its own kit) on PATH: the test says "ok, no other kit on PATH", though that kit shadows the helper inside Claude's Bash
tool, the exact case the test exists to catch. Should: only this plugin's own folder name, or a byte-identical copy, counts as ours.
fix_hint: Remove the */plugins/core/bin/kit alternative in a follow-up once setup --global has run (a fix item), or now if the gate is run after it.
pass_cases: 1. PATH with a dir ending plugins/core/bin holding a different `kit`: the test FAILs and names it.
2. PATH with plugins/relay/bin/kit of this or another checkout: passes.
3. PATH with a byte-identical copy of bin/kit elsewhere: passes (cmp).
reason: Fixer kept the kit-name exemption until the live PATH moves after the merge; follow-up fix item. Agree: removal before setup --global would break the gate.
findings.summary: kit-name test now accepts any program at a path ending plugins/core/bin/kit, a transition-only exemption that stays for good
